# Managed Run Workspace Lifecycle
Kosmic previously had file-hygiene prose but no enforced ownership or lifetime mechanism for scratch files. The governing concept is a **managed run**: Kosmic-created scratch lives below the active Git worktree's `.tmp/kosmic/`, carries deterministic retention, and records related Git status at start and finalization. Story 043 delivered the foundation: `skills/scripts/kosmic_runs.py` resolves the descriptor-anchored, fail-closed run root (only Git worktrees, root `.tmp/` ignore rule required, no-follow owner/mode/type/device checks), and the checked-in versioned migration inventory classifies all fourteen production temporary-path callers and all eight scratch-policy consumers with a source-policy audit test that rejects new unexplained entries.

Stories 044-048 and 052 delivered the initial lifecycle in `skills/scripts/kosmic_runs.py`: strict porcelain-v2 Git snapshots with before/after path classification; versioned manifests, private handle files, terminal receipts, operation records, and bounded rotating history written through descriptor-relative atomic replacement with required fsync; a double-forked session-detached holder holding `fcntl.flock` for the run's active lifetime and serving an abstract-namespace control socket authenticated by peer UID plus a compared token; `begin_run`/`finish_run`/`extend_run`/`promote_file`/`report_runs` as the five public operations; deterministic diagnostic/disposable/extended-diagnostic retention with the 72-hour failure window and seven-day extension cap; and the journaled planned→quarantined→deleted→recorded owner cleanup transaction with idempotent recovery. The `scratch` CLI verbs and automatic command integration (validate, review, check-completion, install, provenance) expose the same interface. The skill-prose cutover (story 053), publication markers (story 056), and destructive `gc --apply` (story 050) remain correctly undelivered.

Cleanup authority remains narrow. `gc --apply` now selects only report-identified valid expired immediate run children, reuses the journaled quarantine transaction, and records before/after Git deltas; active locks, grace candidates, malformed entries, wrong-owner paths, and unsupported cases remain report-only. `startup_collect` is an adapter over that same transaction, bounded to four entries or 256 MiB per automatic command invocation, and reports remaining eligible work without changing the primary command result on maintenance failure. Destination-sibling staging remains under the atomic-publication module because same-filesystem replacement and recovery have different invariants.

The approved requirements are in the [Managed Run Workspaces PRD](../subprojects/feature-prd-managed-run-workspaces/specs/prd.md); the approved holder, descriptor-anchored path, Git snapshot, cleanup transaction, and promotion designs are in the [Architecture](../subprojects/feature-prd-managed-run-workspaces/specs/architecture.md). Stories 044–048, 050, 052, and 054 are implemented and awaiting the required convergent Standards/Spec/security review. Stories 051, 053, and 056 remain gated on their validated Task P proposals and Maintainer approval.

# Projection audience routing

## Behavior (v3.0.0)

`collect_projection_plan` in `skills/scripts/kosmic_project_skills.py` admits only stable, non-expired, non-`usage_stale` notes and routes them by Audience Scope:

- `audience: usage` and `audience: both` → Usage package only.
- `audience: development` → Development package only.
- Missing `audience` → unscoped; Development-only until reviewed.

Consequence: a `both` note is **not** copied into the Development package. The Development router instead carries a textual instruction to load the Usage companion for consumer and shared behavior (`router_text`; codified in `references/task_project_skills.md` invariant: "Development projects stable `audience: development` notes and requires Usage for consumer and shared behavior").

## Change direction

The route-graph redesign (project `both` notes into Development routes, intent-keyed routers) was drafted and then **abandoned on 2026-09-02** before implementation; see the archived [PRD](../specs/archive/2026-09-02-prd-route-graph.md) and [Architecture](../specs/archive/2026-09-02-architecture-route-graph.md). The routing behavior described above therefore remains current. The active improvement direction is WikiSkill-style experience compilation (see [PRD](../subprojects/experience-compilation-adapting-wikiskill-into-kosmic/specs/prd.md)).

# Quick Task: Package-consistent link rewriting in projection

## Scope

- `projected_reference` in `skills/scripts/kosmic_project_skills.py`: body links whose target is not projected into the same Skill Pair package are demoted to bold plain text; same-package links kept verbatim; rewriting skips code fences, external schemes, fragments, non-Markdown targets.
- `generate` prints a stderr warning listing demoted links.
- Tests in `tests/test_project_skills_cli.py` (new class).
- Doc line in `references/task_project_skills.md` + one Principles bullet in the stable usage note (triggers ledger publication entry on regenerate).

## Out of scope

- Cross-package linking (companion-skill naming already covers it); validation failures; draft projection.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Same-package link between two stable usage notes survives verbatim in both references.
- [ ] Stable note linking a draft note (or a stable note in the other package) → link demoted to `**Text**` in the projected reference.
- [ ] `generate` warns on stderr naming demoted targets; no warning when nothing demoted.
- [ ] Ledger gains a publication entry for the changed usage note after regenerate; `validate` exit 0.

## Rationale

WikiSkill principle (arXiv 2608.27454): a delivered knowledge package is internally consistent by construction — its navigation derives from shipped content, not the vault superset. Kosmic's router already does this; reference bodies violated it (three dangling links in the first published pair).

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest tests.test_project_skills_cli` — all green.
- Regenerate + `validate` on the kosmic vault; confirm dangling links gone in `skills/kosmic-usage/references/cli-projection-commands.md`.

# Quick Task: Failure-Derived Procedure Proposals

## Request

Incorporate the ABINIT calibration lesson into Kosmic: repeatedly failed work that yields a general invariant, recovery, and verification matrix is a signal to consider a procedure proposal; it is not automatic promotion.

## Scope

- Add the failure-derived admission rule to Task 9 and Task P.
- Make the root Kosmic Task P routing state the rule concisely.

## Out of Scope

- Changing proposal schemas, CLI behavior, resolver ranking, or artifact-role vocabulary.
- Promoting any ABINIT candidate or creating a Task P artifact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Task 9 distinguishes one-off incidents from evidence supporting a procedure candidate.
- [x] Task P requires a generalized invariant, recovery, reproducer/verification matrix for failure-derived candidates.

# Skill Proposal: Projection CLI Extension Conventions — Projection Sufficiency

## Problem

Task 9 distillation captured these into `notes/cli-extension-conventions.md`, promoted to stable the same day (confidence 0.8). Task P now requires a disposition for this stable CLI-extension Pattern: create one procedural skill, update one existing skill, or `no_action`.

## Evidence

- **Pattern (curated, sha-pinned in the inputs manifest)**: `notes/cli-extension-conventions.md` — `type: Project Knowledge`, `audience: development`, `status: stable`, `usage_stale: false`, `evidence: [evidence/2026-09-02-experience-compilation-impl/session-record.md]`. Four principles: structural exclusion beats filtering (evidence packs and `impact.md` live as siblings of `notes/`; `validate_notes_bundle` and `collect_projection_plan` walk only `notes_dir`); gates run before early returns (`check_completion`'s evidence gate sits before the `if not affects_interface: return`, pinned by a test exercising the early-return path); append-only state appends only after success (ledger written strictly after `publish_directory` succeeds and only for the canonical root, tested via `KOSMIC_FAIL_STAGE` injection); optional frontmatter is absent-compatible (`evidence:`, `evidence_packs:` absent ≡ no-op). Details: Project-root-relative evidence paths; six fixed ledger fields separated by ` | `; re-read the target region before every line anchor. - **Evidence pack** `evidence/2026-09-02-experience-compilation-impl` (kind: execution): `session-record.md` documents the TDD run (18 new tests written first → 11 failing → 66/66 OK), the as-built designs (structural exclusion, gate placement, append-after-publish ledger), and the raw process observations above. # Skill Proposal: Extend Atomic Publish Tree With Staging Markers and Detection

## Problem

`publish_tree` creates its backup sibling with `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".kosmic-publish-backup-", dir=destination.parent)` and relies entirely on in-process `except`/`finally` for cleanup. Exception-path rollback is proven, but a crash inside the transaction window (SIGKILL between `os.replace` calls) bypasses both handlers and strands the sibling with no ownership metadata. Stories 056 and 051 therefore require versioned markers with bounded, attributable status for every destination-sibling stage and backup, report-only detection in the initial release, and destructive recovery only behind a later evidence gate.

Task P search-first resolution against the pinned inventory: `reuse` cannot satisfy the contract because the pinned routine has no marker emission and no detection surface at all; `create` is barred because an owning module exists and the lifecycle note reserves destination-sibling staging under the atomic-publication module ("same-filesystem replacement and recovery have different invariants"); `keep_as_prose` is barred because marker lifecycle and bounded-state classification are deterministic mechanics with a repeatable trigger, typed inputs/outputs, explicit invariants, expected failures, behavioral evidence, and owning domain `kosmic`. The procedure resolves to `extend`, reconsidering the accepted 2026-09-07 `reuse` decision on materially new crash evidence.

## Evidence

From the pinned 2026-09-15 behavioral validation (code state `git_head c52ab6a15b2dab0df9cbd450a76fcdc386612cdb`):

- **Rollback-success baseline**: Python-level failure injection (`KOSMIC_FAIL_STAGE=after-backup`) inside `publish_tree` propagates the exception, restores the prior canonical tree byte-identically, and the `finally` clause removes the backup sibling — the existing rollback contract holds and must be preserved unchanged.
- **SIGKILL stranded-sibling baseline**: a child process killed on the first `os.replace` after backup creation leaves the prior canonical tree intact but strands an empty, unattributable `.kosmic-publish-backup-<random>` sibling with no marker, phase, owner, or expiry metadata; nothing in the current system can detect, attribute, or bound it. This is the concrete gap; it is materially new relative to the 2026-09-07 reuse pack, which contained no crash-ownership scenario.
- Supporting context: the managed-run lifecycle (Stories 044–048, 052; full suite 394 tests OK) already established the staged-destructive-capability precedent (`scratch gc --apply` exits 2 `GC_APPLY_DISABLED`) and deliberately excludes destination-sibling staging from run cleanup authority.

## Applicability

The marker and detection contract applies to every `publish_tree` destination-sibling stage and backup — all four consuming callers (`generate`, `migrate_notes_bundle`, `update_mathdocs`, `generate_library`) and any future consumer of the routine. Detection is destination-scoped and report-only; interpretation of reported states, content approval, and the decision to act on a report remain outside the routine. Destructive recovery applies only after the separately gated Story 051 release.

## Behavioral Validation

Candidate paths: [pending_tests/kosmic/2026-09-15-atomic-publish-tree-recovery/candidate/kosmic_routines.py]

Baseline: KOSMIC_FAIL_STAGE=after-backup restores the prior canonical tree byte-identically and removes the backup in finally; SIGKILL after backup creation strands an unattributable sibling. Candidate: marker v1 precedes destructive publication steps, destination-scoped detection reports active, grace, expired, malformed, or ambiguous without mutation, and existing rollback and one-visible-tree behavior remain intact. Acceptance requires failing-first marker-schema, bounded-state, destination-scope, no-mutation, one-visible-tree, and crash-phase tests in the declared execution Evidence Pack.
## Proposed Change

Extend `kosmic/atomic-publish-tree` in `skills/scripts/kosmic_routines.py` (owning procedure `kosmic/development/atomic-skill-publication`) with three additions; the existing `publish_tree` signature and caller-visible rollback behavior are unchanged.

1. **Marker schema v1** — every destination-sibling stage and backup the transaction touches carries a marker file written before any destructive step, with fields: `schema: kosmic.publish-marker/v1`, `operation_id` (unique per publication attempt), `destination` (resolved destination identity), `source_git_sha256` (source Git hash recorded at begin), `phase` (advancing across the transaction checkpoints: backup-open, prior-tree-saved, staged-installed, committed), `created_at`, `grace_expires_at` (= `created_at` + 24 h, the abandoned-candidate grace), and `retire_by` (= `created_at` + 7 d, the maximum retention bound). Markers live inside the reserved sibling directories and are removed by normal `finally` cleanup, so the one-visible-tree publication invariant is preserved.
2. **Destination-scoped report-only detection** — a read-only query taking a caller-supplied destination, examining only exact reserved sibling names of that destination (never a glob over the parent), returning per-sibling typed records classified `active`, `grace`, `expired`, `malformed`, or `ambiguous`, with no mutation and no destination lock. The initial release explicitly rejects `restore`, `finish`, `retire`, and general-glob cleanup operations, failing closed in the `GC_APPLY_DISABLED` pattern.
3. **Separately gated recovery authority (Story 051, dormant here)** — destructive recovery is declared in this contract but activates only after a later evidence gate: caller-supplied destination plus exact reserved siblings only, destination lock acquired, Story 056 markers validated, restore/finish/retire proven against old/new canonical state with exactly one valid canonical tree visible at every observable point, and ambiguous, malformed, active, unrelated, wrong-owner, and unsupported candidates remaining report-only. Story 056's initial release ships markers and detection only.

## Routine Candidate

Repetition: Four known sibling-staging callers stage under the destination parent on every publication — python:kosmic_project_skills:generate, python:kosmic_project_skills:migrate_notes_bundle, python:kosmic_project_skills:update_mathdocs, and python:kosmic_shared_library:generate_library; each call is a repeatable crash-exposure trigger.

Contract: Typed inputs publish_tree(staged: Path, destination: Path, managed_paths: Sequence[str] | None = None) -> None (unchanged) plus a new detection query (destination: Path) -> tuple[SiblingState, ...] with typed per-sibling state records. Invariant: exactly one canonical tree is visible at every observable point (s² = s; mixed visibility 0; visible count 1), preserved under marker writes, normal finally cleanup, and — once gated in — every recovery branch.

Expected failures: Marker-less reserved sibling (crash before marker write) reports malformed or ambiguous and is never silently deleted; unreadable or wrong-schema marker reports malformed; reserved-name sibling whose destination identity does not match reports ambiguous (report-only); staged tree missing raises RoutineError (existing); wrong-owner or unrelated candidates stay report-only; any destructive operation requested in the initial release is rejected fail-closed.

Leverage: One extension at the single publication seam covers all four callers and every future publish_tree consumer; managed-run reporting can surface sibling states without owning them; Stories 056 and 051 share this one decision; the marker gives crash forensics (operation, owner, phase, age, bounds) that anonymous backup debris cannot.

## Baseline vs Candidate

| Dimension | Baseline (pinned coordinate `44e467e8…`) | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exception rollback | Byte-identical restore; backup removed by `finally` (proven) | Unchanged; regression-pinned by the three existing routine tests |
| Crash (SIGKILL) mid-transaction | Prior tree survives; stranded anonymous sibling — undetectable, unattributable, unbounded | Stranded sibling carries marker v1; detection reports bounded, attributable state with 24 h grace and 7 d retention |
| Detection | None | Destination-scoped, report-only, five-state classification, no mutation |
| Recovery | None | Declared but dormant; activated only after the Story 051 evidence gate |
| One-visible-tree | Holds on success and rollback; crash leaves prior tree plus debris | Holds in all cases; markers live inside reserved siblings |

## Risks

- **Marker-write window**: a crash between sibling creation and marker write leaves a marker-less reserved sibling; detection must classify it `malformed`/`ambiguous` rather than assume safety — mitigated by marker-before-any-destructive-step ordering and fail-closed classification.
- **Shared-seam regression**: the extension touches the transaction used by all four callers; mitigated by the existing rollback regressions plus new failing-first marker-schema, bounded-state, destination-scope, no-mutation, and one-visible-tree tests, with injected crashes at each publication phase.
- **Destructive authority**: recovery can delete trees; it remains dormant until the separate gate proves every-phase crash convergence, unrelated-sibling safety, and wrong-owner refusal.
- **Clock dependence**: grace and retention classification read marker `created_at`; classification is report-only in the initial release, so skew cannot cause mutation.
- **Inherited**: cross-filesystem rename behavior remains unexercised; callers must keep staging under the destination parent to preserve same-filesystem atomic replacement.

# Skill Proposal: Managed Run Orchestrator Step and Lifecycle Reference Cutover

## Problem

The Kosmic skill teaches scratch hygiene as prose only. `skills/SKILL.md` carries a "File Hygiene Before Coding and Before Final Status" section, echoed by seven other inventoried policy consumers, prescribing ad hoc `.tmp/<task-slug>/` placement, manual classification, and prose-only cleanup duties. Stories 044–048 and 052 delivered an executable managed-run lifecycle (lease-backed begin/finalize/status, deterministic retention, mandatory Git-state records, journaled owner cleanup), yet the orchestrator skill contains no step that uses it. Two policies now compete, and agents still have no checkable begin/finalize operation. Story 053 declares `proposal_required: true` for exactly this cutover.

## Evidence

From `evidence/2026-09-15-managed-run-lifecycle/behavioral-validation.md` (code state `c52ab6a1`):

- Suites: focused lifecycle suite `tests.test_kosmic_runs` 74 tests OK; full suite 394 tests OK (baseline 348).
- Live CLI across independent processes: `scratch begin` → JSON `code OK`, private `handle_file`, run tree mode `0700`; the detached lease survives the beginning process (independent probe `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` → `EWOULDBLOCK`); `scratch status` → `{"code":"OK","live":true,"state":"active"}`; `scratch succeed` from a third process removes the run and records cleanup with `git_before_sha256`/`git_after_sha256`; `scratch gc --apply` correctly refused (`GC_APPLY_DISABLED`).
- Promotion: `scratch promote` from a second process verifies bytes/hash and records the before/after Git delta.
- Automatic command integration: `validate` leaves zero run directories (disposable run finalized and cleaned); `provenance` leaves the worktree untouched; non-Git creation fails closed with `NO_GIT_WORKTREE`.
- Trigger evidence: the current SKILL.md hygiene section plus seven other policy consumers still prescribe ad hoc `.tmp/<task-slug>/` and `.scratch/{skill-name}` placement with prose-only cleanup; the orchestrator has no mandatory managed-run step.

Notes: `notes/managed-run-workspace-lifecycle.md` (draft; governing concept "managed run"; eight scratch-policy consumers inventoried with a source-policy audit) and `notes/cli-projection-commands.md` (stable; documents the `scratch begin|succeed|fail|extend|promote|status|gc` adapter and automatic command integration). Proposal history: `impact.md` records no rejected fingerprint for this target; the accepted 2026-09-07 atomic-publish-tree proposal is a shared-routine reuse with no overlap. Mechanics classification: the deterministic lifecycle already exists in `skills/scripts/kosmic_runs.py` and the `scratch` CLI — reuse, no new routine; remaining skill content (when to begin/finalize, durable-rule boundaries) is judgment prose. Story 053 declares `routine_edge_change: false`; no routine action is required.

## Proposed Change

One atomic `update` to `skill://kosmic` (sketch; final prose authored in Story 053 implementation):

1. **SKILL.md — replace "File Hygiene Before Coding and Before Final Status" with one mandatory step** using the leading concept `managed run`:

   > **Managed Run Before Scratch (MANDATORY).** Before creating any scratch, runtime, or generated output, begin a managed run:
   > `python3 {KOSMIC_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/kosmic_project_skills.py scratch begin --project {VAULT}/Projects/{TARGET} --purpose {task-slug}`
   > **Done when**: the JSON reply has `code: OK` and a run path under `.tmp/kosmic/runs/`; write all scratch inside that run. `NO_GIT_WORKTREE` → stop: the vault must sit in a Git worktree whose root ignores `.tmp/`.
   > **Before final status**: finalize with `scratch succeed` (or `scratch fail`). **Done when**: JSON `code: OK`; a successful diagnostic/disposable run leaves no run directory and history carries its start/final Git snapshots.
   > Durable files never live in run scratch: source/docs in the project tree; `pending_tests/<project>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>/original-paths/<original-path>` with `MANIFEST.md`, committed before finishing; Evidence Packs under `evidence/`; specs and project logs under their own governance.

2. **Add one lifecycle reference** `references/managed_run_lifecycle.md` owning path layout, retention classes and extension, promotion, recovery, cleanup, and the destination-sibling atomic-publication exception. SKILL.md names it once; agents load it only when lifecycle detail is needed (progressive disclosure, NFR-MRW08).

3. **Remove the duplicated scratch mechanics from the other seven inventoried policy consumers in the same cutover**: `skills/README.md` "File Hygiene" (collapse to the pointer), `references/task_implement_story.md` Step 3.1 (drop its four hygiene bullets; point at the mandatory step), `references/task_quick_task.md` Step 5 (same), and the remaining ADR/spec and inventory consumers (FR-MRW22). Each consumer keeps only audience-specific durable rules (pending tests, Evidence Packs, specs, logs). The duplicate-policy source check stays red until no competing scratch policy remains.

## Applicability

The step is procedural and reusable: every Kosmic task that creates Kosmic-owned scratch — story implementation, quick tasks, generated outputs, diagnostics — repeats the same begin/write-inside/finalize mechanics with checkable outcomes. It applies only to Kosmic-created scratch below the active Git worktree's `.tmp/kosmic/`; it does not govern durable files (source, `pending_tests/`, Evidence Packs, specs, project logs), user-created files, or destination-sibling atomic-publication staging. Branch-specific lifecycle detail is progressively disclosed via `references/managed_run_lifecycle.md`. Overlap analysis: no competing skill exists — this update removes the eight duplicated policy occurrences instead of adding a ninth.

## Behavioral Validation

Candidate paths: [pending_tests/kosmic/2026-09-15-managed-run-workflow/candidate/SKILL.md]

Invariant scenario: a fresh-context agent performing work that creates scratch begins a managed run, writes scratch only below its returned .tmp/kosmic/runs path, and terminally succeeds or fails it. Observable criterion: both commands return code OK and history contains the start and final Git snapshots. Baseline is prose-only ad hoc scratch; candidate is the executable lifecycle plus one leading workflow instruction and progressive reference.
## Baseline vs Candidate

| Behavior | Baseline (current hygiene prose) | Candidate (one step + one reference) |
|---|---|---|
| Scratch placement | Ad hoc `.tmp/<task-slug>/`, `.scratch/{skill-name}`, repo roots | One resolved run under `.tmp/kosmic/runs/` from `scratch begin` |
| Begin | None; classify-by-prose before creating files | Checkable: JSON `code: OK` + run path |
| Lease/ownership | None | OS lease spans tool calls (probe `flock` → `EWOULDBLOCK`) |
| Finalization | "Delete before review" prose duty | Checkable: `succeed`/`fail` → `code: OK`, run removed, history record |
| Git-state record | Manual `git status --short` classification only | Mandatory start/final porcelain-v2 snapshots plus cleanup before/after hashes |
| Failure retention | Undefined | Deterministic: diagnostic 72 h, disposable, extension ≤ 7 days |
| Detail location | Duplicated across eight consumers | One SKILL.md step + `references/managed_run_lifecycle.md` |
| Durable rules | Mixed into hygiene prose | Preserved as explicit distinct rules (pending_tests, Evidence Packs, specs, logs) |

## Risks

- **Cutover completeness**: eight consumers must change atomically; a partial cutover leaves competing policies. Mitigation: keep the Story 043 source-policy audit red until zero unexplained entries (FR-MRW20/22) and migrate every consumer in one reviewed change.
- **Reference breakage**: removing the hygiene section breaks consumers citing it by title (`task_implement_story.md` 3.1, `task_quick_task.md` 5); the same change rewrites those references and bumps the skill version (consumer interface change).
- **Over-reach**: the run lifecycle must not absorb durable governance; `pending_tests/`, Evidence Packs, specs, and logs keep their own rules (FR-MRW18), explicitly preserved above.
- **Agent bypass**: a fresh-context agent may skip the step; the checkable JSON criterion and finalization history record make omission detectable at review.
- **Scope creep**: the initial release refuses destructive `gc --apply` (`GC_APPLY_DISABLED`); the step text must not promise it. Non-Git vaults fail closed (`NO_GIT_WORKTREE`) — the README must state that prerequisite.
- **Skill surface**: one added mandatory step; net length decreases because the larger hygiene section and its echoes consolidate into one reference.

# Proposal: create shared routine kosmic/day-delta-harvest

## Problem

Collecting "what observably changed in a vault on date D" now exists only
inside the Kosmic dream collector (`kosmic_dreams.collect_harvest`). The same
union — Git window commits with before/after blobs, frontmatter dates, and
dirty state — is useful outside dreams: Task 4 review sweeps, evidence-pack
freshness audits, and any cross-project day report.

## Proposed Change

Extract the collector's source-union core (timezone/date resolution, window
commit walk, diff-tree parsing, frontmatter pass, dirty classification,
canonical file entries) into a shared routine declared in
`kosmic_dreams.py` and registered as `kosmic/day-delta-harvest`. The dream
harvest becomes the routine's first caller and keeps its Dream-specific
extensions (open work, flags, read set) local.

## Evidence

- Repetition across three dream records: candidates logged in
  `dreams/2026-09-16.md`, `dreams/2026-09-22.md`, and `dreams/2026-09-23.md`.
- Implementation proven by 42 dream tests and four real vault harvests.
- Task 3 search: no existing routine covers day-delta collection
  (`query-routines` returns only `kosmic/atomic-publish-tree`).

## Routine Candidate

Repetition: Three independent dream records (2026-09-16/22/23) required
  the same day-delta union; Task 4 review sweeps and evidence-freshness audits
  re-derive it ad hoc.
Contract: Inputs `vault: Path`, `date: str | None`, `zone: str | None`;
  output canonical JSON bytes of {window commits with before/after blobs,
  frontmatter dates, dirty classification}; deterministic, no network, pure
  read over the Git repository.
Expected failures: no Git repository under the vault; malformed or
  missing dates; timezone resolution failure; dirty-state race during harvest
  (entries flagged dirty, not silently dropped).
Leverage: one canonical collector replaces per-consumer reimplementation;
  byte-identical outputs pinned by the existing 42 dream tests keep the dream
  caller and future consumers aligned.

## Applicability

Procedural and deterministic: fixed trigger (collect day-delta for date D),
typed inputs/outputs, byte-pinned invariants. Dream-specific judgment (open
work, flags, read set) stays prose and local; only the source-union mechanics
are shared. No overlap: routine inventory holds only
`kosmic/atomic-publish-tree`.

## Behavioral Validation

Candidate paths: [pending_tests/kosmic/2026-09-24-day-delta-harvest/candidate]
Scenario: harvest the same vault/date before and after extraction; invariant:
canonical JSON bytes byte-identical, 42 dream tests pass; baseline =
pre-extraction `kosmic_dreams.py`, candidate = routine-backed collector;
evidence pack recorded at acceptance under
`evidence/2026-09-24-day-delta-harvest/`.

## Scope

- Add `KOSMIC_ROUTINES` declaration + regenerate inventory; no behavior change
  to dream outputs (byte-identical harvest before/after extraction).

## Risks

- Routine edge adds inventory governance; extraction must not alter canonical
  JSON bytes (pinned by tests).

# Architecture: Dream Reflection

## System Overview

Dream is a Task D workflow over deterministic CLI seams. `dream-harvest`
begins a managed run, snapshots the canonical dream tree into run-owned
staging, and emits a complete, versioned reflection contract. Task D reads
only that contract's hash-pinned `read_set` and writes only two run-owned
inputs: a candidate dated record and proposed idea entries. `dream-publish`
derives every path from the authenticated handle, merges those inputs into the
staged tree, redacts, validates, checks concurrency/replacement preconditions,
atomically promotes the tree, and finalizes the run. The CLI never performs
language-model judgment; Task D never discovers the delta or copies canonical
state.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Task D: dream] --> B[dream-harvest]
    B --> C[Managed run + staged base + DreamHarvest]
    C --> D[Agent reads immutable read_set]
    D --> E[Candidate record + idea inputs]
    E --> F[dream-publish derives run-owned paths]
    F --> G[Merge + redact + composite validation + base checks]
    G --> H[publish_tree atomically replaces dreams root]
    H --> I[Run succeeds with Git evidence]
    V[(Pinned vault state)] --> B
    D -.read-only.-> R[Harvest-selected files/blobs]
    H -.only write surface.-> O[(memnotes/dreams/)]
```

## Technical Decisions (ADRs)

### AD-DR1: Observable target-day union, not an exact edit-time claim

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Git records commit time, frontmatter records declared knowledge
time, and dirty state records only the present. No source reconstructs an
unrecorded historical edit exactly.

**Decision**: Harvest resolves the effective timezone as explicit
`--timezone` first, otherwise the host's resolvable IANA timezone; failure to
resolve one fails closed. Omitted `--date` means the preceding calendar date
in that timezone, including DST boundaries. From captured `HEAD`, harvest
walks all reachable commits (all parents; deterministic topological/time/SHA
ordering) whose committer instant falls in that UTC-converted date window.
Merge commits use first-parent tree diffs; shallow history emits a coverage
warning.

The authoritative Markdown surfaces are `Projects/**`, `Skills/**`, and
vault-root Markdown. `dreams/**` is excluded from the target-day delta to
avoid self-input, except that prior Skill Candidate sections are collected
explicitly. Under `--project`, project-local discovery is limited to the
selected Project while shared `Skills/**` and root records remain included
and are labeled shared.

Harvest unions: (1) ordered Git before/after observations; (2) one
metadata-only pass selecting `created == date` or `updated == date`; and (3)
porcelain-v2 staged, unstaged, untracked, renamed, and deleted state under the
same surfaces. Each file has old/new paths, status, available blob IDs and
hashes, and origins `git|frontmatter|dirty`. Untracked Markdown may be read for
frontmatter; dirty deletions carry no current content. Coverage records
commits, HEAD, shallow-history warning, dirty classes, and exclusions. The
product says “observable target-day delta,” never “exact edits.”

**Consequences**: Late commits and untracked dated notes remain observable;
missing metadata stays an explicit limitation. Content reads remain bounded.

**Alternatives Considered**: Git alone, mtimes, or frontmatter alone—all lose
a required class of observable work.
---

### AD-DR2: Vault-level dream surface and validator

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Dreams span projects and therefore cannot be validated by
project-scoped `validate --project`.

**Decision**: `memnotes/dreams/` contains only `{YYYY-MM-DD}.md`, `index.md`,
and `ideas.md`. New `validate-dreams --vault` validates:

- record filename/date and required frontmatter/section schema;
- relative links and allowed paths;
- exactly one reverse-chronological index row per date;
- unique `{date}-{slug}` idea IDs and valid `merges:` targets;
- absence of `.tmp/kosmic/` paths and known secret-bearing field labels.

Dream records are records, not atomic Project Knowledge, so they are outside
projection and unattributed-note checks. `dream-publish` always validates the
staged tree before promotion.

**Consequences**: Validation ownership is explicit and independent of project
selection. Unknown children fail closed.

**Alternatives Considered**: Extending project validation (wrong scope),
overloading `validate-library` (wrong domain), unvalidated records (not
acceptable).

---

### AD-DR3: Typed harvest is the complete reflection contract

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Reflection needs judgment, but its discovery inputs must be
bounded and auditable. The original delta-only schema could not support open
work, flags, historical transitions, or repetition evidence.

**Decision**: `dream-harvest` emits `kosmic.dream.harvest/1` containing:

- provenance, canonical ordering rules, coverage, and exact Git before/after
  blob observations;
- per-project changed files, selected log items, status changes derived from
  ordered old/new frontmatter blobs, evidence, and impact entries;
- `open_work` from authoritative records: nonterminal stories, epics, and
  quick tasks under `Projects/*/specs/**`; draft PRD/Architecture approval
  gates; and pending Skill Proposals. Terminal `done|rejected|deprecated`
  records are excluded. `--project` applies before enumeration;
- deterministic knowledge checks, link index, candidate evidence, and a
  hash-pinned reflection `read_set`;
- canonical dream-tree base digest and per-date generated-record state.

Knowledge-check algorithms are fixed: a selected log item is a Markdown list item in the target-date log not already containing `[Extracted]`; a changed draft is frontmatter `status: draft`. Harvest performs one complete link-only scan of every Markdown file in the AD-DR1 authoritative surfaces at captured HEAD overlaid with enumerated dirty state. It uses the existing relative Markdown-link parser and NFC-normalized vault-relative paths; anchors do not affect file identity and nonportable Wikilinks are unsupported. `uncited-draft` means zero backlinks in that complete snapshot. Declared stale means `usage_stale: true` or `stale_after < target date`; evidence-order emits when a valid MANIFEST date is strictly later than a citing note's valid `updated`. Missing or malformed required metadata is a validation finding, not silently ordered. Multiple citations emit one structured finding per note/pack pair.

Task D may read only current paths or materialized immutable Git blobs listed
in `read_set`, after hash verification. Possible contradiction remains
judgmental and must link both inputs.

**Consequences**: Open work begun before the target day is included; historical
status transitions do not depend on current files; mechanics/judgment blame is
clean.

**Alternatives Considered**: Agent-led discovery or a delta-only contract.

---

### AD-DR4: Advisory-only mutation boundary

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Dream must propose without bypassing Task Review, Task 9, Task P,
or Shared Skill Library governance.

**Decision**: Task D writes only the designated candidate dated record and proposed idea-input file inside its managed run. Knowledge Flags, Today actions, and Skill Candidates are prose with evidence links. A Skill Candidate needs two evidence references and a proposed Task P scope. Cross-project/shared candidates remain judgment outputs and can enter the library only through a later explicit Task P action. `dream-publish` alone rebuilds the index and merges ideas; no note, log, spec, status, marker, proposal, or library file is mutated.

**Consequences**: The workflow is useful without acquiring hidden authority.

**Alternatives Considered**: Auto-proposals and `[Extracted]` writes (rejected
by user choice and governance).

---

### AD-DR5: Managed-run handshake and whole-tree publication

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Agent judgment spans more than one CLI process, but scratch ownership, publication paths, cancellation, retry, and crash cleanup must remain authenticated and deterministic.

**Decision**:

1. `dream-harvest` begins the existing managed run, authenticates vault/run
   binding, copies the canonical `dreams/` tree into a run-owned stage using
   no-follow containment checks, and writes harvest/control data there. Its
   compact stdout contains the public run ID, private handle path, and harvest
   path; stage paths are derived later from the handle, never caller-selected.
2. Task D writes only the designated run-owned candidate-record and idea-input files. The candidate must omit `generated_content_sha256`; Task D never reads or mutates the copied base tree.
3. `dream-publish --handle ... [--replace]` resolves all paths from the authenticated handle; rejects escapes, symlinks, devices, FIFOs, wrong owner/mode, and vault mismatch; rechecks `read_set`; deterministically merges inputs; redacts; canonically serializes the final record; computes and inserts `generated_content_sha256`; validates against the staged dream tree overlaid on hash-pinned external link targets; compares the canonical tree with `base_dreams_sha256`; then calls `publish_tree`.
4. Identical idea IDs deduplicate only when normalized entries match; a nonidentical collision fails closed. Index rebuilding is CLI-owned.
5. Success finalizes the run. Validation/input errors leave the active run retryable. Concurrency drift is retryable only after a new harvest. `dream-abort --handle ...` and holder expiry provide authenticated, idempotent failed finalization for cancellation or agent crash.

**Consequences**: No agent runtime is embedded in Python, caller-supplied paths
cannot escape the run, and record/index/ideas publication cannot split.

**Alternatives Considered**: A fictitious full-pipeline CLI, agent-owned base copy, three promotions, or direct writes.

---

### AD-DR6: Rerun, filter, ordering, and deferred behavior

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: One record per date collides with project filters, reruns, and manual edits; a whole-tree concurrency digest cannot distinguish reviewed prose from its last generated ancestor.

**Decision**:

- `--project` filters project evidence/open work while retaining labeled shared
  evidence; it still writes the one canonical date record.
- Every generated record stores `generated_content_sha256`. `dream-publish` alone generates and inserts it after merge and redaction from the exact canonical bytes specified by the record schema; candidate input containing the field fails. Harvest only verifies the persisted field using that same byte algorithm. Match means generated state; mismatch means manual divergence and sets `replacement_requires_replace: true`. First creation has no prior digest; legacy records without the field require `--replace`.
- `--replace` authorizes replacing the diverged dated record only. It never
  bypasses whole-tree base drift, read-set drift, validation, or idea-ID
  collision checks.
- `index.md` is rebuilt from date filenames newest first. Idea IDs dedupe
  exactly; near duplicates use explicit `merges:` links.
- Weekly rollup and configurable aging are deferred. Cross-project skill
  candidates remain judgment over supplied evidence.

**Consequences**: Rerun and manual-edit behavior is testable, filtered runs
cannot fork records, and reviewed prose cannot be erased silently.

**Alternatives Considered**: Per-filter records, append-only reverse indexes, unconditional overwrite, or a whole-tree digest standing in for record ancestry.

---

### AD-DR7: Secret and provenance boundary

**Status**: Proposed

**Context**: Agent-authored prose may accidentally preserve run handles,
scratch paths, or credentials.

**Decision**: Harvest exposes a public run ID but marks the private handle path
as control data excluded from the reflection `read_set`. Before validation,
`dream-publish` applies the existing Kosmic purpose-redaction rules to staged
Markdown. Validation rejects `.tmp/kosmic/`, private-handle field labels, and
known token field labels. `produced_by` contains `dream/{public-run-id}` only.
Task D instructions prohibit copying credential values even when present in a
source note.

**Consequences**: Permanent provenance remains useful without publishing run
capabilities or scratch topology. Heuristic rejection supplements—not
replaces—the Task D rule.

**Alternatives Considered**: Validator-only token regexes (false confidence)
or no automated guard.

## Data Models

### DreamHarvest

```json
{
  "schema": "kosmic.dream.harvest/1",
  "date": "2026-09-16",
  "timezone": "Europe/Brussels",
  "head": "{sha}",
  "source_commits": ["{sha}"],
  "project_filter": null,
  "coverage": {"shallow": false, "dirty_classes": [], "warnings": [], "excluded_surfaces": ["dreams/"]},
  "base_dreams_sha256": "{sha256-or-empty-tree-digest}",
  "replacement": {"existing": true, "generated_match": false, "requires_replace": true},
  "projects": [{
    "project": "kosmic",
    "files": [{"old_path": "...", "new_path": "...", "status": "modified", "old_blob": "{sha}", "new_blob": "{sha}", "origins": ["git"]}],
    "log_items": [{"id": "{stable-id}", "ref": "..."}],
    "status_changes": [{"path": "...", "from": "in_progress", "to": "done", "old_blob": "{sha}", "new_blob": "{sha}"}],
    "open_work": [{"kind": "story", "path": "...", "status": "blocked", "blocker": "approval", "updated": "2026-09-16"}],
    "evidence_packs": ["Projects/kosmic/evidence/.../MANIFEST.md"],
    "impact_entries": ["Projects/kosmic/impact.md#..."]
  }],
  "knowledge_checks": [{"kind": "unextracted-log", "subject": {"path": "...", "id": "..."}, "evidence": [{"path": "...", "sha256": "..."}]}],
  "link_index": [{"source": "...", "target": "..."}],
  "candidate_evidence": [{"kind": "prior-dream|routine", "ref": "...", "summary": "..."}],
  "read_set": [{"kind": "path|git-blob", "ref": "...", "role": "...", "sha256": "..."}]
}
```

All arrays use documented stable sort keys (projects/paths lexical; commits by
topological order then committer instant/SHA; origins by fixed enum order;
findings by kind/subject). Paths are NFC-normalized POSIX vault-relative
strings. Duplicates collapse by typed identity. JSON is UTF-8, sorted keys,
compact separators, and one trailing newline.

### Dream record

Schema `kosmic.dream.record/1` fixes YAML types and enums: ISO date string, IANA timezone string, unique lexical lists for projects/commit SHAs, `project_filter: null|string`, `status: draft`, structured coverage-warning strings, public `produced_by`, and lowercase SHA-256 `generated_content_sha256`. Required H2 sections appear once in the FR-D4 order. `dream-publish` is the sole serializer: frontmatter uses schema key order and canonical scalar/list rendering; the document is NFC-normalized UTF-8 with LF line endings and exactly one trailing newline; body whitespace otherwise remains unchanged. The generated hash covers those final persisted bytes with only the complete `generated_content_sha256` YAML line removed, and is computed after merge/redaction but before final validation and promotion.

### Ideas entry

`- {date}-{slug} — {idea} — trigger: {relative-link} — next: {action} (added {date})`
with optional `merges: {id}`. IDs are immutable; identical normalized entries
dedupe and differing same-ID entries fail.

## API Design

- `dream-harvest --vault {VAULT} [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--timezone IANA] [--project TARGET]`
- `validate-dreams --vault {VAULT} [--root STAGED_DREAMS] [--harvest HARVEST]`
- `dream-publish --vault {VAULT} --handle HANDLE [--replace]`
- `dream-abort --vault {VAULT} --handle HANDLE --reason TEXT`

Task D (`dream`) composes these commands and owns reflection prose. External
links are checked against the live vault only after their harvested hashes are
reverified; staged internal links resolve against the candidate tree. No-delta
is valid because open work is still reported. Invalid date/timezone/project,
shallow required history, handle/path/schema/hash/base drift, or malformed
inputs fail closed.
## Test Strategy

| Level | Approach | Coverage |
|-------|----------|----------|
| Unit | Fixture Git repositories, late commits, target-date frontmatter, dirty trees, pinned timezone | Union/origin semantics, deterministic JSON, disclosed coverage |
| Unit | Scripted status/link/evidence fixtures | `open_work` and every deterministic Knowledge Flag oracle |
| Unit | Valid/malformed staged dream trees | Validator paths, schema, ordering, IDs, links, secret/scratch rejection |
| Integration | Harvest → staged reflection fixture → publish; injected digest drift/failure | Managed-run handshake, whole-tree atomicity, rollback, concurrency |
| Integration | Two dates, filtered run, same-date reruns, manual divergence | Reverse index, ideas dedupe, idempotence, `--replace` contract |
| E2E dogfood | Real managed-run release day | Done/In Flight ground truth, late/uncommitted fixture, contradiction links, evidence-backed candidate, zero proposal writes |

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Historical edit time is unknowable without evidence | Medium | Observable-union semantics and explicit coverage warnings (AD-DR1) |
| Metadata pass grows with vault | Medium | Metadata-only single pass; content bounded by `read_set`; future date index if measured necessary |
| Agent reflection varies | Medium | Task D pins evidence rules; dogfood review gates delivery |
| Concurrent/manual dream edits | High | Base-tree digest and explicit replacement semantics (AD-DR5/6) |
| Prose leaks control data | High | Redaction plus fail-closed validation and Task D instruction (AD-DR7) |

## Dependencies

- Shipped managed-run lifecycle and `publish_tree` transaction (Epics 23–25).
- Existing routine query and Task P governance for candidate evidence/routing.
- Existing Markdown/frontmatter parser, purpose redaction, Git snapshot, and
  directory digest helpers.

# Dream Reflection

## Problem Statement

Kosmic accumulates a day of work across projects—log sessions, knowledge notes,
story transitions, evidence packs, and impact entries—but does not read that
work back as a whole. The next session therefore starts without one trustworthy
view of what finished, what remains active or blocked, which knowledge changed,
or which repeated mechanics and ideas deserve follow-up. Task Review performs
interactive knowledge hygiene; Kosmic lacks a whole-vault, backward-looking
reflection workflow over the previous day's observable history.

## Goals

- A user-facing Task D (`dream`) reflects on the target day (calendar yesterday
  by default) across all projects and produces one vault-level record.
- Deterministic CLI mechanics harvest the target-day delta, current open work,
  and bounded knowledge/candidate evidence; agent judgment produces the digest.
- `memnotes/dreams/` holds one record per date, a reverse-chronological index,
  and a cumulative idea backlog.
- Every record states source coverage and answers: what finished, what remains
  in flight (including blockers), what knowledge changed or needs attention,
  and what skills or experiments may be worth pursuing.
- Skill candidates remain advisory and enter Task 9 → Task P → Maintainer
  governance only through a later explicit action.

## Non-Goals

- Automatic modification of canonical skills, Project Knowledge, specs, logs,
  evidence, or status fields outside `memnotes/dreams/`.
- Auto-created Task P proposals or `[Extracted]` markers.
- Per-project dream files; project detail is grouped inside the vault record.
- Scheduled or daemon execution.
- Claiming exact edit-time history when neither Git nor maintained frontmatter
  records it; the dream must disclose such coverage limits.
- Weekly rollups and configurable idea aging in the initial release.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|----|-------------|----------|
| FR-D1 | Task D is the user-facing `dream` workflow. It accepts `{VAULT}`, optional `--date YYYY-MM-DD`, optional `--timezone IANA_NAME`, and optional `--project {TARGET}`. Effective timezone resolves as explicit `--timezone`, otherwise the host's resolvable IANA timezone, otherwise fail closed; omitted date means the preceding calendar date in that timezone. Deterministic CLI subcommands provide harvest and publication; the CLI does not impersonate agent judgment. | must |
| FR-D2 | Harvest computes the union of (a) files changed by target-window commits under tracked vault surfaces, (b) files whose frontmatter `created` or `updated` equals the target date, and (c) relevant dirty files. It records exact source commits, timezone, origin per file, dirty state, and coverage limitations. | must |
| FR-D3 | Harvest emits versioned, typed JSON inside a managed run. It includes changed files, log sessions, story transitions, evidence packs, impact entries, a current `open_work` snapshot, deterministic knowledge checks, an explicit reflection `read_set`, and skill-candidate evidence. | must |
| FR-D4 | Dream records live at `memnotes/dreams/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` with versioned frontmatter `schema: kosmic.dream.record/1`, `type: dream`, `date`, `projects`, `source_commits`, `timezone`, `produced_by`, `generated_content_sha256`, and `status: draft`; required sections are Done, In Flight, Notes Digest, Knowledge Flags, Skill Candidates, Ideas, and Today. | must |
| FR-D5 | Deterministic Knowledge Flags are operationally defined: `unextracted-log` means a selected log item lacks `[Extracted]`; `uncited-draft` means a changed draft note has no Markdown backlink in the harvested link index; `declared-stale` means `stale_after` is past or `usage_stale: true`; `evidence-order` compares MANIFEST `date` with citing-note `updated`. `possible-contradiction` is an agent judgment and must cite both notes. | must |
| FR-D6 | Skill Candidates are listed only in-record. Each candidate cites at least two evidence references from the target-day delta, prior dream candidate sections, or routine-query results, and includes a proposed Task P scope. | must |
| FR-D7 | `dreams/index.md` is deterministically rebuilt with exactly one reverse-chronological row per dream. `dreams/ideas.md` is cumulative; idea IDs are `{date}-{slug}`, exact IDs are unique, and optional `merges:` links near-duplicates identified during reflection. | must |
| FR-D8 | A vault-level `validate-dreams --vault {VAULT}` command validates allowed paths, dream frontmatter/sections, filename-date equality, index uniqueness/order, idea IDs, and links. `dream-publish` invokes it against the staged tree and fails closed. | must |
| FR-D9 | Publication stages a complete candidate `dreams/` tree and atomically promotes it through the existing `publish_tree` path with a base-tree digest precondition. No unrelated vault path changes. | must |
| FR-D10 | Same-date reruns compare the canonical record against its persisted `generated_content_sha256`, which `dream-publish` alone computes after merge/redaction from canonical persisted bytes. Unchanged generated records are replaceable idempotently; manual divergence requires explicit `--replace`. `--project` filters evidence but still produces the single canonical date record and records the filter. Whole-tree base-digest drift always fails and cannot be bypassed by `--replace`. | must |
| FR-D11 | Cross-project repetition detection is judgment-phase, advisory-only: harvest supplies prior candidate/routine evidence, and Task D may surface a Shared Skill Library candidate without modifying library or proposal files. | should |
| FR-D12 | A later release may add `dream --week` and configurable idea aging after at least two real daily dream records exist. | could |

## Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|----|-------------|----------|
| NFR-D1 | For identical vault state, target date, timezone, and project filter, harvest JSON is deterministic and offline. Reflection is explicitly judgmental and is not claimed deterministic. | must |
| NFR-D2 | Reflection reads only the harvest plus paths and immutable hashes in its `read_set`; it writes only the staged `memnotes/dreams/` tree. | must |
| NFR-D3 | Harvest may make one metadata pass and one link-only content pass over Markdown in the authoritative vault surfaces. Other full-content reads are bounded to the target delta, open-work records, deterministic flag evidence, prior dream candidate sections, and routine-query results. | must |
| NFR-D4 | Before publication, existing Kosmic redaction rules remove known token/handle fields and scratch paths; permanent records may contain public run IDs only. Validation rejects `.tmp/kosmic/` paths and known secret-bearing field labels. | must |
| NFR-D5 | Dream records are Obsidian-readable, use relative Markdown links, and conform to the declared dream schema. | must |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] A dream over a real prior workday includes every observable changed memnote, states any coverage gap, and matches completed/in-flight story ground truth including work begun before that day.
- [ ] A seeded uncommitted target-date note is harvested via frontmatter and tagged with its origin.
- [ ] Each deterministic Knowledge Flag passes its operational oracle; a seeded contradiction links both notes and is labeled judgmental.
- [ ] A genuine repeated mechanic appears as an evidence-backed Skill Candidate without creating a proposal file.
- [ ] Two dates and a same-date rerun produce a unique reverse-chronological index and duplicate-free ideas backlog; manual divergence requires `--replace`.
- [ ] `validate-dreams` passes valid staged/canonical trees and fails closed on malformed records, secrets, scratch paths, duplicate dates, and index drift.
- [ ] Full suite, completion gates, and adapter byte checks remain green after delivery.

## Resolved Questions

- Weekly rollup and configurable aging are deferred beyond the initial release.
- Idea identity is deterministic `{date}-{slug}`; near-duplicate merging remains agent judgment with explicit links.
- Knowledge Flags are read-only findings; remediation is prose guidance and never mutates source records.
- Task D owns judgment; the CLI owns deterministic harvest, validation, and publication.

# Story 059: Dream Vault Schema and Validator

## User Story

As a vault maintainer,
I want first-class validated dream records,
So that reflection history remains linkable, safe, and structurally trustworthy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `validate-dreams --vault` accepts only dated records, `index.md`, and `ideas.md` under the dream root and enforces `kosmic.dream.record/1` types, enums, headings, filename/date equality, and relative links.
- [x] The validator enforces one reverse-chronological index row per dated record and unique, well-formed idea IDs/merge targets.
- [x] Composite link checks validate staged internal targets plus hash-pinned external targets and fail on drift.
- [x] Canonical record serialization and `generated_content_sha256` generation/verification follow AD-DR6 byte-for-byte.
- [x] Scratch paths and known private handle/token field labels fail validation; valid public run provenance passes.
- [x] Separate candidate-record and idea-input schemas enumerate agent-writable fields; reject generated digests, target identity/date, provenance/run identity, index rows, and other publisher-owned fields.

## Tasks

### Phase 1: Research

- [x] Reuse evidence, index, OKF, canonical scalar/list, digest, and redaction conventions.
- [x] Specify the exact record/index/ideas grammars in Technical Notes.

### Phase 2: Tests (TDD - Write First!)

- [x] TEST-059-1: Valid and malformed record/frontmatter/section/path fixtures.
- [x] TEST-059-2: Index ordering/uniqueness and idea collision/merge fixtures.
- [x] TEST-059-3: Canonical hash, external-link drift, scratch, and secret-label fixtures.

### Phase 3: Implementation

- [x] IMPL-059-1: Add dream record/index/ideas parsers, serializer, and validators.
- [x] IMPL-059-2: Add `validate-dreams` CLI and staged composite-view validation.
- [x] IMPL-059-3: Add redaction and generated-content digest helpers used by publication.

### Phase 4: Review

- [x] All tests pass
- [x] Consumer-interface completion gate passes with stable usage knowledge
- [x] Standards and Spec review completed

## Routine Decision

Dream validation is tied to Kosmic vault schemas and remains project-local CLI
infrastructure; no Shared Routine edge is introduced.

## Technical Notes

The validator is vault-scoped, not an extension of project-scoped `validate`. It defines both untrusted agent-input schemas and final canonical schemas; `dream-publish` must call the same implementation and derive every publisher-owned field itself.

| Existing parser can express the fixed YAML types | ⬜ | Projection CLI parser |
| Existing redaction policy is callable before serialization | ⬜ | Managed-run implementation |

# Story 062: Dream Run Recovery and Concurrency

## User Story

As a Task D operator,
I want explicit retry, abort, race, and crash semantics,
So that every managed dream run has one safe terminal result.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Completion fails unless Story 061 is `done`; the run state table defines active, publishing, retryable-input-error, retryable-validation-error, reharvest-required, succeeded, failed/aborted, and expired outcomes.
- [x] The publication commit point serializes publish/publish, publish/abort, abort/expiry, and retry races so exactly one terminal receipt wins and repeated terminal calls return that receipt idempotently.
- [x] Input/validation errors retain an active retryable run; evidence/base/concurrency drift requires a fresh harvest; partial publication failures follow `publish_tree` recovery and cannot be retried until reconciled.
- [x] `dream-abort` authenticates the handle, stops the holder, records failed finalization, and owns cleanup; holder expiry/reaping yields the same bounded terminal semantics after agent crash.
- [x] Tests pin exit/result codes, receipts, cleanup ownership, and same-date outcomes for identical output, divergent generated output, manual divergence, and `--replace`.

- [x] Specify the serialized commit boundary and race outcome table.

- [x] TEST-062-2: Publish/publish, publish/abort, abort/expiry, crash, and partial-publication races.
- [x] TEST-062-3: Cleanup ownership and fresh-harvest requirements after every failure class.

# Architecture — Experience Compilation

Implements [PRD](prd.md) (approved 2026-09-02). Bound by repo ADRs [0002](../../../../docs/adr/0002-single-evidence-layer.md) (single evidence layer) and [0003](../../../../docs/adr/0003-wrap-never-vendor-wikiskill.md) (wrap, never vendor).

## Vault layout (per Project)

```
{VAULT}/Projects/{TARGET}/
├── notes/                      # OKF bundle — unchanged, only projected layer
├── evidence/                   # NEW — excluded from OKF validation + projection
│   └── {YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}/
│       ├── MANIFEST.md
│       └── *.md, *.jsonl       # immutable payloads
├── impact.md                   # NEW — flat append-only ledger, excluded from projection
├── specs/                      # specs (research/ absorbed per ADR-0002 → evidence/, FR-011)
└── log/                        # unchanged
```

## Components

### AD-1 Evidence storage and exclusion (FR-001, FR-002)

Evidence and `impact.md` live at Project root, **siblings of `notes/`**, not inside it. Consequence: exclusion is structural, not filtered — `validate_notes_bundle` (scripts/kosmic_project_skills.py:338) walks only `notes_dir`, and `collect_projection_plan` (:450) reads only `notes_dir`; neither ever sees them. The single code change is any directory-walk over the Project root (project discovery, `migrate`) tolerating the two new entries. No projection path is touched.

`MANIFEST.md` frontmatter: `kind: execution | research`, `produced_by`, `date`, `summary` (≤2 lines). Body: one line per payload file naming its role. No hashes — git is the hash layer.

### AD-2 `evidence:` note frontmatter (FR-004)

`parse_markdown` already exposes `document.metadata`; validation hooks into the existing per-note loop in `validate_notes_bundle` (:340-343): for **stable** notes only, every `evidence:` entry must resolve relative to the Project root. Drafts may dangle (pending packs). Additive and optional — existing notes without the key are unaffected.

### AD-3 Impact Ledger appends (FR-005, FR-006)

Two append points, both programmatic:

- **Publication**: at the end of `generate`, after atomic publication succeeds, append one entry per changed note: `date, kind: publication, targets: [note paths], refs: {old→new source hashes from Projection Provenance}, outcome: published, reason: ""`. Hashes come from the existing provenance pipeline — no new hashing.
- **Decision**: Task 7 review appends `date, kind: decision, targets: [note paths], refs: story id, outcome: accepted|rejected, reason: ≤1 line`. Appended by the reviewing agent per the task doc — the CLI *validates* but does not author decision entries (human-gate invariant).

`validate` parses `impact.md` when present: fixed 6 fields, known kinds/outcomes, ISO dates; malformed → failure (FR-006).

### AD-4 Completion gate (FR-007)

Extends `check_completion` (:1244) after the existing `consumer_interface_change` block, mirroring its shape: optional work-item frontmatter `evidence_packs: [slugs]`; absent → no gate (backward compatible); present → every slug must resolve to `evidence/{slug}/` and have ≥1 **draft or stable** note linking it via `evidence:`. Failure message names the orphaned slug.

### AD-5 Task 9 — Distill (FR-003)

Pure procedure doc, no code: `skills/references/task_distill.md`, catalogued in `SKILL.md`. Inputs: declared packs + existing notes. Procedure = Appendix E.2 analysis rules (root cause WHY, success-vs-failure, action patterns, exact commands, success + failure patterns, 10–30 lines, never-duplicate, index entry = problem+root-cause+fix). Outputs: draft notes / updates / deprecations via Task 2 conflict policy; promotion only through human review. Attribution header cites arXiv 2608.27454 and the pinned MIT repo revision. Executable by any agent reading the doc alone (NFR-004).

### AD-6 Retention flag (FR-008)

Task 4 doc gains one review item: list packs not referenced by any note's `evidence:` key and older than 3 months (pack date from directory name). Flag-only; no CLI enforcement, no deletion.

## Data flow

```
work item ──declares──> evidence pack ──Task 9 (Maintainer)──> draft note (evidence: links)
                                                                │ human review (Task 7)
                                                                v
                                            stable note ──generate──> Skill Pair + ledger entry
                                            rejected change ─────────> ledger decision entry
```

## Migration (FR-011)

One-time, this vault: move the two `specs/research/` memos to `evidence/2026-09-02-{slug}/MANIFEST.md + payload`, set `kind: research`; update PRD `linked_research` and specs INDEX links. Other vaults: no note edits required anywhere (all new keys optional).

## Test strategy

Extend `tests/test_project_skills_cli.py` (pytest, tmp-vault fixtures per existing convention): pack-manifest validation, `evidence:` resolution (stable dangling → fail; draft dangling → pass), ledger schema (malformed → fail), `check-completion` gate (orphan slug → fail; linked draft → pass; no declaration → pass), Project-root walk tolerance.

## Out of scope

Stage 2 wrappers (separate approval per ADR-0003); any projection/routing change; OKF modifications.

# Experience Compilation: adapting WikiSkill into Kosmic

## Problem Statement

Kosmic's knowledge system captures Project Knowledge only when the agent discretionally decides to (Task 2 triggers exist but nothing enforces them), keeps no raw material behind notes, and has no memory of which knowledge changes were published or rejected across sessions. The result is the observed behavior: notes and skills are rarely written or updated, and rejected ideas get re-litigated.

WikiSkill (arXiv 2608.27454) validates the fix experimentally: a persistent knowledge layer that compounds from execution experience, separated from the skills built on it, improved skill evolution by +15.0 average points; its absence is the dominant ablation. Its loop machinery now exists as MIT-licensed, third-party code (`github.com/ashutoshsinghpr7/wikiskill`), but that implementation is benchmark machinery (auto-graded task packs, score gating, plain-markdown wiki) — not an Obsidian/OKF-conformant project-knowledge system with human gates.

## Decisions (settled in grilling session 2026-09-02, ADRs 0002–0003)

- **One evidence layer** (ADR-0002): research discovery and execution outcome are two kinds of the same concept — the Evidence Pack. `specs/research/` is absorbed.
- **Vocabulary imported as roles**: Pattern (the role of a distilled note), Maintainer (the agent executing Distillation), Impact Ledger (mirrors `skill-impact.md`). `vault`/`notes/` untouched; task names stay verb-first.
- **Task 9: Distill** is the only *gated* extraction (Task 2 stays opportunistic, Task 4 periodic).
- **Enforcement is mechanical**, not discretionary: a CLI gate, not a checklist.
- **Stage 2 posture pinned** (ADR-0003): wrap the pip package on demand; never vendor.

## Goals

- Make knowledge capture **mechanical, not discretionary**: distillation runs as a defined post-work step driven by captured evidence, enforced by the existing completion gate pattern.
- Add the three missing WikiSkill mechanisms to the Kosmic vault, OKF-conformant: Evidence Packs, Distillation (Task 9), and the Impact Ledger.
- Reuse the verified Appendix E.2 Maintainer analysis procedure with attribution.
- Preserve every Kosmic invariant: authoritative OKF notes bundle, deterministic stdlib CLI, human approval gates, atomic publication, projection pipeline untouched.

## Non-Goals

- Benchmark scoring loops, validation-score gating, or autonomous skill-proposer agents (the grader is the test suite + Task 7 review; the gate is human).
- Changing the projection/audience/routing model (route-graph direction abandoned 2026-09-02; archived under `specs/archive/`).
- Auto-stable notes or auto-publication: Distillation output is always `draft` until human review.
- Projecting Evidence Packs or the Impact Ledger into generated skills.
- Vendoring third-party code into this repository.

## Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|----|-------------|----------|
| FR-001 | Evidence layer: `{VAULT}/Projects/{TARGET}/evidence/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}/` — one pack per work item (story, quick task, or standalone investigation); immutable and append-only; `MANIFEST.md` with frontmatter `kind: execution \| research`, `produced_by`, `date`, `summary` (≤2 lines) and a body file list with a one-line role per file; no per-file hashes (git is the hash layer) | must |
| FR-002 | Evidence is excluded from OKF bundle validation and projection exactly like `log/`; the Projection CLI ignores it | must |
| FR-003 | Task 9 (Distill): a Maintainer agent analyzes declared Evidence Packs plus existing notes. Procedure adopts the Appendix E.2 analysis rules wholesale — root cause (WHY, not WHAT), success-vs-failure comparison, action patterns not error messages, exact command sequences, both success and failure patterns, 10–30-line notes, never-duplicate (update existing notes with new evidence), index entry states problem + root cause + fix. Dropped from upstream: the JSON output contract and wholesale index rewrite (the OKF index is maintained per Task 2). Outputs: draft notes, updates, or deprecations; conflicts follow Task 2's conflict policy; deprecation stays human-gated | must |
| FR-004 | Additive optional note frontmatter `evidence: [paths]` (relative to Project root); CLI validates entries resolve for stable notes; drafts may reference pending evidence | must |
| FR-005 | Impact Ledger `{VAULT}/Projects/{TARGET}/impact.md`: flat, append-only; entry = 6 fixed fields (date, kind `publication\|decision`, targets, refs, outcome, reason ≤1 line); no prose. `generate` appends publication entries (changed note paths, old→new source hashes); Task 7 review appends decision entries for knowledge changes | must |
| FR-006 | Ledger is excluded from projection; `validate` fails on malformed ledger entries | must |
| FR-007 | Completion gate: work items declare `evidence_packs: [slugs]` in frontmatter (optional; absent = no gate); `check-completion` fails when any declared pack lacks a draft-or-stable note linking it via `evidence:` — mirrors the `consumer_interface_change` gate pattern | must |
| FR-008 | Task 4 review flags unreferenced Evidence Packs older than 3 months; nothing is ever auto-deleted or auto-archived | must |
| FR-009 | Attribution: prompt/procedure text adapted from WikiSkill carries attribution to arXiv 2608.27454 and the MIT repo, with the pinned upstream revision recorded in the Kosmic release | must |
| FR-010 | Stage 2 (optional, separately approved): transcript-capture adapters wrapped on demand from the installed `wikiskill` pip package (ADR-0003); no vendoring | could |
| FR-011 | Migration: existing `specs/research/` memos become `kind: research` Evidence Packs; specs INDEX and spec frontmatter links updated | must |
| FR-012 | Docs updated: `SKILL.md` task catalogue (Task 9), `README.md`, `references/task_add_note.md`, `references/task_implement_story.md`, `references/task_quick_task.md`, `references/task_review.md` (retention flag), `docs/` | must |

## Non-Functional Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Priority |
|----|-------------|----------|
| NFR-001 | Stage 1 uses only the Python 3.11+ standard library; no runtime dependency on the third-party repo | must |
| NFR-002 | All CLI checks remain deterministic and offline | must |
| NFR-003 | Evidence Packs are plain files (Markdown + JSONL), git-friendly, Obsidian-browsable outside `notes/` | should |
| NFR-004 | Distillation must be executable by any capable coding agent reading the task doc alone — no hidden prompt state | must |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] A real story produces an Evidence Pack; Distillation yields a draft note with valid `evidence:` links; review promotes it to stable; `validate` passes.
- [ ] A work item with `evidence_packs:` declared but no linking note fails `check-completion`; adding the draft note passes it.
- [ ] `generate` publication and a Task 7 reject decision each append correct 6-field ledger entries; malformed entries fail `validate`.
- [ ] A stable note with an unresolvable `evidence:` path fails `validate`.
- [ ] `kind: research` pack (migrated memo) is accepted by the same validation as `kind: execution`.
- [ ] Full `tests/` suite passes with new coverage for FR-002, FR-004, FR-005, FR-006, FR-007.
- [ ] Attribution + pinned revision recorded for every adapted text.

## Open Questions

- [ ] None blocking. Ledger split cadence (flat vs per-year) revisited if `impact.md` grows unwieldy; Stage-2 wrapper interface sketched at architecture time.
